## 2. The 11 rules files

### `overrideStyling.md` (280 lines) — the authority on the build approach

The single most prescriptive file. **The styling hierarchy, in reach-for order (`:12-37`):**
1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, **never a raw `fontSize`**; all 22 Handover text styles live in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never a bare Chakra/theme token key** (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) even though it resolves identically — house-style, for unambiguity at the call site. Mechanically enforced for recipes by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`; **that guard cannot see the same mistake in a JSX/`sx` prop** — that half is manual (`:24-27`).
3. The component's own theme config — `theme/components/<name>.ts` **or** co-located `<name>.css.ts`.
4. `sx` for a one-off prop-system gap.
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes).

**"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file"** (`:39`). One standing exception: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional `BTN_HEIGHT_LG/SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`. `npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) greps for exactly this across `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**`; a hit is downgraded when the surrounding comment contains `provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow: <reason>`. **Not wired into CI** (`:50`, restated `:227-237`) — 14 pre-existing violations need triage first.

**Units (`:58-70`):** `rem` for anything scaling with root font-size (type + spacing, WCAG 1.4.4); `px` for hairline geometry that must *not* scale (borders, focus-ring offsets); `em` only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`).

Other hard constraints:
- **Alias tier is a reference, not a copy** (`:72-87`) — semantic tokens read from primitive consts; `zimmTokens.ts` derives everything except 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases.
- **One canonical styling surface per component type** (`:89-104`) — a component's theme config is the single source of truth; **do not also give it a `.zimm-*` global class**, because a static class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`. `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*`; use Chakra `<Button>`.
- **Importing an already-overridden component (`:106-134`) — a real trap.** From component A, import an already-overridden B by **relative path** (`'../swatch-group'`), *not* the SFCC base path, because the `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real app build — Storybook aliases straight to `node_modules` and Vitest doesn't touch it, so a base-path import silently renders/tests the **unstyled base SFCC version**. Known unfixed instance: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import (`:126-130`).
- **Component-local tokens (`:136-165`)** — reference the foundation entry as `var(--zimm-*)`, not `2`, not `'0.5rem'`, not the bare key. **Responsive steps are explicit media queries keyed off `BP`, not Chakra's array shorthand** — the guard walks responsive arrays and fails every element. No existing foundation entry and no confirmed Figma value → **leave it inherited; don't invent a number**.
- **SFCC bridge pattern (`:173-193`)** — if SFCC's own base components import it, the default export stays a faithful undecorated port (full prop surface, same `forwardRef`); Zimmermann styling goes behind a named export (the `product-tile` `CardBaseline` split).
- **Co-location governance (`:197-250`)** — `theme/components/` is Tier 2 gated to the UI designer, but CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` routes a co-located recipe to the owning squad only, dropping the designer gate. Explicit **known inconsistency flagged not resolved** (`:218-225`): `zimmButton.css.ts`'s unapproved provisional constants are no longer designer-gated while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. Cross-file shared values go in a small module that stays in `theme/components/` (e.g. `footerShared.ts`).
- `:252-266` logs known gaps; `:268-281` logs follow-up initiatives (per-component CSS loading; `globalStyles.ts` adoption is near zero).
- ⚠️ `:4` cross-references `./overrides.md` — **that file does not exist in `.claude/rules/`**.

### `css.md` (74 lines)

Day-to-day companion. `:9-46` Tokens — no hardcoded hex, no px spacing, no raw font sizes; shows three code examples including the ❌ bare-token case. `textStyle` is the one deliberate bare-key exception because there's no `var()` substitute for the composite expansion (`:26-31`). `:33-46` states plainly that the raw-value half has a script but **no CI gate and no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule**, while the bare-token half **is** enforced via `recipeGuards.test.ts` on every `npm run test`.

`:48-74` `.scss` only when Chakra props are insufficient, with 6 hard constraints: filename matches the component exactly; **scoped and co-located only, no global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/`**; **nesting depth ≤ 3**; **no ID selectors**; **no `!important` without an inline reason comment**; prefer `sx` or a theme variant over a new `.scss` file.

### `components.md` (167 lines)

- **Components (`:11-47`):** named export matches folder name, no anonymous default exports; props type named `<Component>Props`; **placement default = top of the component file**, move to `types.ts` only on *shared consumption* (not line count alone); JSDoc required on ≥2-caller components, every exported hook, and non-obvious utils; `onEventName` callbacks; optional props use `?`, no `| undefined` unions.
- **Accessibility (`:35-47`) — "mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`":** every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` fine for decorative); every `IconButton` (incl. `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs `aria-label`; any non-native element with `onClick` (`div`/`span`/`Box`/`Flex`/`Stack`/`VStack`/`HStack`/`Grid`/`Text`) needs a `role`, plus `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown` for real operability.
- **Composition (`:49-104`):** ~150 lines / ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity as a self-check — **explicitly NOT ESLint-enforced today** (`:56-58`). **Container/presentational separation (`:62-90`)** is the big one: anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props and calls **no** data-fetching hook (SDK *or* React Query); fetching lives in `overrides/app/pages/` or a container. Narrow exception for Context-backed app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) — with a precise warning that their no-Provider behaviour **differs**: `useUiCopy` degrades to fallback text, `useIntl` **throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by base SFCC `_app` not `_app-config`, so Vitest tests must wrap it. Extract-to-hook triggers: ≥2 related `useState` that change together, or any `useEffect` with a non-trivial dep array/cleanup; ≥4 `useState` is a coarse "stop and ask".
- **Hooks (`:106-113`):** `.ts` only (no JSX), exported name matches filename, params and return typed, JSDoc with `@returns` mandatory.
- **Storybook (`:116-166`):** story **required** for anything exported from its folder under `components/` or `pages/`; **not required** for single-parent internal sub-components; pages get one full-assembly story. Seven-category table (`:137-143`) `Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/` with a tiebreaker rule and ✅/❌ examples. Every file has a `Default` export; named exports for meaningful states only; `play` only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting.

### `testing.md` (432 lines) — the largest rules file

- **Three layers, no duplication** (`:3`), with a long carve-out (`:5-20`): this is **not** license to skip a component's own test file because a hook test or a parent's `play` covers it transitively. Resolve duplication by *scoping what the file asserts* (mock the hook/child proven elsewhere; test only this component's render-branch/event-wiring contract). Reference: `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx`. Exempt: components with no branching at all (`BottomBar`).
- Layer table `:22-26` — Vitest / Storybook `play` / Playwright, each gated on every PR via `qa.yml`; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**`.
- **What to test / skip (`:32-44`):** ✅ data mapping, integration boundaries (Global-e pricing/tax, checkout ownership branching, consent gating), complex state, refactor-invisible logic. ❌ re-exports, visual snapshots in Vitest, the framework itself.
- **Vitest (`:46-97`):** co-located, **`.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`**; describe/test, Arrange-Act-Assert, behaviour-named tests, `vi.clearAllMocks()`. Mock the smallest surface; **MSW allowed for cross-module integration tests but never in production paths**; don't mock the thing under test. **Known gap (`:79-86`): `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest** — mock it at the smallest surface; unfixable from a test file because the SVG transform lives in Tier 1 `vitest.config.ts`. Commerce SDK hooks need `QueryClientProvider` + `CommerceApiProvider` via a `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/`.

## 3. `.claude/hooks/`

Wired in `settings.json:2-61`. Five hooks total — four scripts plus one inline command.

| Event | Matcher | What runs | Blocking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PreToolUse` | `Write\|Edit\|NotebookEdit` | **Inline command**, `settings.json:9` — `git branch --show-current`; if `develop` or `main`, echoes `BLOCKED: …` and `exit 1` | **Yes — hard block** |
| `PreToolUse` | `Write\|Edit\|NotebookEdit` | `hooks/tier2Warn.sh` | No (`exit 0`) |
| `PostToolUse` | `Write` | Inline: `node_modules/.bin/prettier --write "$f"`, `statusMessage: "Formatting new file with Prettier..."` (`:24-25`) | No |
| `PostToolUse` | `Edit\|Write` | `hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (`:34`) — **file does not exist**; the `[ -f … ] &&` guard makes it a silent no-op | No |
| `PostToolUse` | `Edit\|Write` | `hooks/registryUpdate.sh` | No |
| `PostToolUse` | `Write` | `hooks/testFileRemind.sh` | No |
| `Stop` | — | `hooks/session-reflect.sh` | **Yes — `decision: "block"`** |

**`tier2Warn.sh` (70 lines)** — parses `tool_input.file_path` from stdin JSON via inline python3, then regex-matches six Tier 2 groups and prints `⚠️ TIER 2 — <group>` + owner + "Required: second developer review before this PR merges to develop." Groups at `:33`, `:40`, `:46`, `:52`, `:58`, `:64`. ⚠️ **The theme branch is broken: `:52` matches `/theme/components/project/`, but `protectedFiles.md:49` defines the Tier 2 path as `overrides/app/theme/components/` — that warning can never fire.** Also missing from the script vs `protectedFiles.md`: `uiCopyProvider/`, `globalStyles.ts`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/`.

**`registryUpdate.sh` (45)** — scoped to `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `overrides/app/routes.*` (`:23-24`); skips `.test.`/`.stories.`/`ContentfulDefinition`; resolves node via PATH → NVM sourcing → newest `~/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/node`, silently exits if none; then runs `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs --file="$file_path"` (`:45`). This is what keeps `.claude/registry/` live.

**`testFileRemind.sh` (55)** — scoped to `/app/{components,hooks}/`, JS/TS source only, skips test/spec/stories/ContentfulDefinition. Checks all four `.test.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}` variants and, if none exist, prints `🧪 No test file found for X` + the expected path + **"Run /code-quality to audit test coverage before opening a PR."**

**`session-reflect.sh` (45)** — the most consequential hook. Re-entry guard on `stop_hook_active`; exits early if `git status --porcelain` is empty; otherwise emits `{decision: "block", reason: …}` which **forces Claude to keep working before the session can end**. The instruction: write **a single** proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/<ts>-<branch>.md`, and **"Do NOT edit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .docs/memory/*, .docs/prd/*, or .claude/rules/* directly — those are Tier 1 / human-owned"** (`:28`). Each section must carry target path + rationale tied to something that actually happened + a concrete diff. Candidate list at `:33-42`. If nothing changed, write a one-line "No doc updates proposed." **This is the project's doc-drift mechanism, and it is proposal-only by design.**

## 4. `.claude/registry/`

Five generated markdown tables + two hidden JSON caches. Every `.md` carries the header `> Generated by \`node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs\` — do not edit manually.` plus a timestamp and `> Base: @salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`.

| File | Lines | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `components.md` | 101 | Component, Origin (Base/Override/Custom), Path, Props, **Tier**, **Squad**, **Consumers**, Last touched, Description |
| `hooks.md` | 71 | Hook, Origin, Path, Description, Consumers, Tier, Squad, Last touched |
| `utils.md` | 39 | Utility, Origin, Path, Exports, Last touched, Description |
| `pages.md` | 25 | Page, Origin, Path, Squad, Tier, Last touched |
| `routes.md` | 26 | URL, Component, Page folder, Source (Override/Inherited), Squad, Tier — generated from `overrides/app/routes.tsx` + inherited base routes |

**Generation** — `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (header at `:1-16`): full run (`npm run generate:registry`, also run on `postinstall`), incremental `--file=PATH`, or `--fresh` to ignore caches. It scans `overrides/app/` **and** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` (`:27-28`), which is why the tables carry `Origin: Base` rows for components that were never overridden. It computes and stamps Tier and Squad onto every row — i.e. the registry is the **materialised join of the tier/squad rules against the actual file tree**.

**Caches:** `.baseCache.json` (52 KB, `{version, schema:3, components:73, hooks:57, utils:30, pages:15}`, rows of `{key,name,path,props,desc,consumers}`) caches the expensive upstream scan. `.overrideCache.json` (6 KB, `{components,hooks,utils}` keyed by repo-relative path → `{hash, consumers, lastTouched}`) uses a **sha1 content hash** so a row's consumer count is only recomputed when its own source actually changed (`generateRegistry.mjs:47-60`). The script's own comment documents a fixed bug where incremental mode used to blank every untouched row in a category to `—`.

**Consumption** — two skills read it and both degrade gracefully: `feature-spec/SKILL.md:39` ("_If `.claude/registry/` exists_, read components.md, hooks.md, utils.md", else `find`), and `generate-changelog/SKILL.md:49-53` (`git diff BASE..HEAD -- .claude/registry/` to detect new assets, else `git log --diff-filter=A`). Its stated purpose (`generateRegistry.mjs:5-7`) is *"structured markdown tables that Claude Code reads instead of grepping the codebase."*

### (b) NOT covered anywhere in `.claude/`

**Jira / Confluence research** — **not covered.** `qa-generate/SKILL.md:26-28` asks the developer to *paste* the story key, title and acceptance criteria by hand; no skill calls a Jira tool. `feature-spec` sources requirements from `.docs/prd/` files, never from Jira. The MCP plumbing exists and is allowlisted read-only (`settings.local.json:10-12,31-32`) but **nothing in `.claude/` uses it**. No skill fetches a ticket, reads a spec page, summarises epic scope, or reconciles a ticket against `.docs/`.

**Figma design verification** — **not covered at all.** Zero occurrences of "figma" in `.claude/skills/` or `.claude/hooks/`. It appears only as prose in rules (`frozenFiles.md:42` "design-parity review against Figma"; `overrideStyling.md:150,168,260` "no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet"). Rules *depend* on a confirmed Figma value existing ("don't invent a number", `overrideStyling.md:167-171`) but there is **no mechanism to fetch one, compare a built component against a frame, or record the token→Figma mapping.** This is the largest structural hole given how token-centric `overrideStyling.md` is.

**Multi-agent build orchestration** — **not covered.** Three skills spawn parallel agents (`feature-spec` 3, `code-quality` 4, `generate-changelog` 3) but **all of them are read-only research/audit agents**. No skill dispatches parallel *implementation* work, splits a spec across agents, manages worktrees, or reconciles concurrent edits. `feature-spec` deliberately terminates at "here is a prompt to paste into the next session."

**PR authoring** — **not covered.** `/pr-checklist` generates description *text* and README.md:53 states "nothing is posted for you". No skill runs `gh pr create`; `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule 15 forbids opening a PR without an explicit ask. Nothing handles: branch push, base-branch selection, draft vs ready, reviewer/CODEOWNERS assignment, linking the Jira issue URL that `pr-checklist:49-50` says is required, or labels.

**Responding to CodeRabbit** — **not covered by any skill.** `AGENTS.md` has a detailed mandate ("Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review": reply in-thread to *every* finding, fixed or not; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count; for a not-fixing decision cite the specific rule/doc so CodeRabbit's learning stops re-flagging it). **No skill implements it.** `/code-review` is the generic vendor skill and is purely local-diff CLI — it has no concept of a GitHub PR review thread, `gh pr comment`, resolving conversations, or this repo's rule files as justification sources. `rules/testing.md` shows the practice happening manually (`:275`, `:280`, `:320`, `:362` — "CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-26").

**Reviewing OTHER people's PRs** — **not covered.** Every quality skill is scoped to *your own* branch: `code-quality` diffs the current branch, `pr-checklist` diffs the current branch, `code-review` reviews the local working tree. Nothing takes a PR number, checks out or fetches someone else's diff, applies the tier/squad rules to it, checks Tier 1/Tier 2 reviewer requirements from the reviewer's side, or drafts review comments. Tier 2's whole premise — "requires a PR review from a developer who is not the author" (`protectedFiles.md:3-4`) — has **zero tooling on the reviewer's side.**

**Deploys / release cuts / tagging** — **rules-only, no skill.** `rules/tagging.md` fully specifies the taxonomy, the tag-only-push procedure, `gh workflow run deploy-*.yml -f ref=…`, `versionGuard.mjs check|record`, and rollback — but there is **no `/cut-release`, `/tag`, `/deploy`, or `/promote` skill.** `/generate-changelog` covers only the notes, and even then *proposes* rather than runs `gh release create`. Nothing verifies pre-cut readiness (clean `git pull --ff-only`, annotated tag, guard state, environment reviewers configured — which `tagging.md:81` flags as an unmet prerequisite for gated rollback), and nothing monitors a deploy run or drives a rollback.

**Sprint ceremonies** — **not covered.** `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` is *read* by `session-start:14`, `feature-spec:20`, `qa-generate:30`, `code-quality:69` and `generate-changelog:62`, and `session-reflect.sh:39` can only *propose* an edit to it. Nothing runs standup prep, sprint planning, backlog grooming, retro capture, sprint rollover (despite `tagging.md:36` referencing auto-cut `sprint/{N}/{date}` tags), or story estimation/status transitions.

**Also uncovered, worth noting for a personal skill set:** the Magento-baseline `# DELTA:` classification loop (`onboarding:211-213` describes it, no tooling); running `npm run audit:tokens` as a pre-PR gate (`overrideStyling.md:42-56` says it must be run manually and is not in CI); the reviewer-side WCAG 2.2 AA verification `pr-checklist:61` puts on a checkbox; and any skill for `npm run env` tier switching beyond onboarding's first-run instructions.
